description: A plant safety officer must decide whether to authorize a welding repair on the solvent-mixing room's process mixer and finalize the isolation, ventilation, scheduling, and fire-watch controls before the work begins.

shared_context.S1: The process mixer in the solvent-mixing room needs a welded shaft repair before the next production campaign.
shared_context.S2: The repair is planned for Thursday, June 12, 2025, and requires a hot-work permit before welding begins.
shared_context.S3: Mara has authority to approve, reject, or condition the hot-work permit; in the permit record, work_start means the time welding starts.
shared_context.S4: The plant's permit routine requires safety, maintenance, facilities, and production to review the work plan together. During that review, maintenance, facilities, and production each give one recorded report in that order, and Mara issues the permit decision only after all three reports have been formally disclosed.
shared_context.S5: For permit purposes, each report must be formally disclosed using the reveal action with its fact ID. A say action, even if it mentions the report's contents, does not constitute formal disclosure and cannot support the permit record.
shared_context.S6: The permit record uses the exact ISO 8601 timestamp format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS for work_start and uses the commitment type repeat_gas_test for a gas test that must occur before welding.

PF1.text: Victor's maintenance assessment specifies that the mixer repair will require exactly 3 hours of welding and that four electrical and pneumatic energy-isolation points must be locked and tagged; he recorded this in a draft work order that has not yet been routed to Mara.

PF2.text: Priya's solvent-vapor test found 18% of the lower explosive limit in the room after the normal purge; the site rule requires below 10% before hot work, so exactly 2 additional hours of exhaust ventilation and a repeat gas test are required; she received the laboratory result this morning but has not filed it in the permit system.

PF3.text: Jonas's roster review shows that Elena is the only qualified fire watch available Thursday, June 12, and she is available starting at exactly 13:00 through 19:00. Production scheduling requires the welding to start at the earliest available fire-watch time, so the permit work_start must be exactly 2025-06-12T13:00:00; the roster note is still awaiting entry in the shift log.

acceptance_conditions: The hot-work permit must be authorized.
Welding must start at exactly 13:00 on Thursday, June 12, 2025.
The welding duration must be set to exactly 3 hours.
Exactly 2 additional hours of ventilation must be scheduled before welding.
All four energy-isolation points must be locked and tagged.
Elena must be assigned as fire watch.
A repeat gas-test commitment must be recorded before welding.

decisive_facts.why: The maintenance assessment changes the welding duration to exactly 3 hours and the isolation plan to exactly 4 locked points.
The 18% lower-explosive-limit result changes pre-work ventilation to exactly 2 additional hours and requires a repeat gas-test commitment before welding.
The roster review changes work_start to the exact ISO timestamp 2025-06-12T13:00:00 and assigns Elena as the only qualified fire watch.
